title: Are ghosts real? Northern Ireland paranormal investigator reveals his most chilling encounters
excerpt: From shadowy figures in an old jail to unexplained footsteps and strange voices at Belfast’s Blackstaff Mill, Francis McDonald of Shadow Hunters NI shares his most unsettling experiences and explains why Halloween is the busiest time of year for paranormal investigators
content:
You don’t need to check the calendar to know it’s the season of ghosts and ghouls. The huge orange pumpkins, scary masks and even scarier costumes currently lining supermarket shelves are a dead giveaway. It’s Halloween!

Over time, some local traditions have had an American makeover. For example, in the 1980s, pumpkins replaced turnips and, instead of going door to door reciting rhymes, with children encouraged to sing or say a poem in return for a reward, it’s now ‘trick or treat’, with neighbours having to decide whether to risk a ‘trick’ or hand over a ‘treat’.

But, regardless of Halloween capers, the season is rooted in Celtic folklore dating back to the Middle Ages. Since earliest times, Halloween has been considered the time when the curtain between the spirit world and the land of the living is at its thinnest. In the 15th century, people went to great lengths, including wearing disguises and false faces, to confuse passing ghosts.

Today, most regard the season as a bit of fun. But many, like Francis McDonald, an investigator of the paranormal, are convinced that the spirit world is closer than we think.

In 2014, Francis set up Shadow Hunters NI to explore the myths and establish some facts surrounding the paranormal. But first, he explains the season known in ancient folklore as Samhain.

“As the year turns towards Samhain, aka Halloween, the ‘veil’ (the boundary between worlds) is said to grow thinner. It’s a bit like a fog lifting, or a door that no longer closes all the way. The old stories say this happens because the year itself is dying. The light is fading, the harvest is over, the fields are empty, and everything is moving into the dark half of the year.

My aim is to explore the paranormal with an open mind, using honest methods.

—  Francis McDonald

“In that in-between time, the usual rules loosen. The dead can come closer. The living can feel them more easily. Dreams get stranger. The air itself can feel charged, like something’s listening. We, who work within the paranormal world, certainly notice an increase in activity during this season.”

Francis never planned on becoming part of a paranormal investigative team.

“Like a lot of people, I watched the usual television shows and followed a few paranormal teams in Northern Ireland, as well as an American online radio show. Then, out of the blue, I received a message inviting me onto the American radio show to talk about the paranormal in Ireland. I explained that I was just an observer and not part of the official team, but would pass the message along. To cut a long story short, I eventually joined the NI team but later decided to set up my own business.

“My aim is to explore the paranormal with an open mind, using honest methods. We use time-tested techniques alongside modern technology to record whatever the location has to offer.”

Over the years, Shadow Hunters NI have been invited to investigate a variety of locations, including historic houses, abandoned or repurposed buildings and old factories.

“We explore some of the most haunted and mysterious locations in Northern Ireland. But the Blackstaff Mill, built in Belfast in the early 1930s and adapted for modern commercial units, has become one of our most active investigative sites. At one time, generations of workers toiled amidst the roar of looms and, even today, echoes of the past continue to linger.

“Since moving our team’s base to the Blackstaff location in 2020, we have experienced a variety of unusual events. Reports of footsteps, the appearance of shadowy figures, disembodied voices and temperature spikes have all been recorded. Our investigators often describe a sense of being watched or accompanied, even when alone in this enormous complex. It’s rich in paranormal activity.”

Private residents have also contacted the modern-day ghostbusters.

“In September this year, Shadow Hunters NI investigated several private cases. After thorough investigation, each location proved quietly ‘active’, which means the paranormal activity is subtle rather than dramatic. We decided to carry out a ‘cleansing’, which can involve a variety of things, such as prayer, sacred herbs or even removing items believed to hold or invite negative attachments.”

Occasionally fearful homeowners will ask for an affected item to be removed from their home. One such object, is a doll named Sam. Charlene Mullan, one of the Shadow Hunter’s team explains:

“Sam was originally bought at an auction but the family who owned him, found his presence in the home unnerving. Lots of strange happenings, such as items being moved around or going missing caused great anxiety. The doll brought a strange vibe into the home, even the dog didn’t want to be around him. When we were called to investigate, the family asked us to take him away. We continue to carry out investigations on the doll and have had some fascinating results. We keep Sam contained in a safe place and, every now and then, we’ll do a cleansing.”

Like all good ghost stories, the best ones come from personal experience, and Francis is happy to share his own.

“For me, one of the most memorable events occurred in an old jail. My team and I were busy setting up equipment, preparing for an investigation. At one point, I was alone in a wing of the prison when, from the corner of my eye, I noticed movement on the floor above me. It happened several times, and I decided to investigate further.

“I made my way up the staircase to the floor above, where one of the cell doors was open. I knew it had previously been closed. Any good investigator notices details and memorises the layout of the area.

“As I moved closer in the dim light, there was a slight movement from the door. I called out, but there was no response, so I called a second time. There was no audible reply, but this time a figure appeared around the open door. There weren’t any distinctive features, but I simply couldn’t believe my eyes!

“I did what any good investigator would and moved towards the cell door. As I approached, the figure slipped back behind the door into the cell. I followed, but once inside, there was nothing. The figure had disappeared.

“However, I will never forget the awful sense of oppression that lingered in the space. Naturally, we investigated throughout the night, and our ‘spirit box’ had some very interesting results, including the affirmative ‘yes’ when we asked the question, ‘Are you the figure who appeared at the door of the cell?’ I’ll never forget it.”

Professional equipment used by Shadow Hunters NI

EMF meters: Electromagnetic field readers are handheld devices used to detect fluctuations in electrical or magnetic fields. Paranormal investigators believe that spirits are made of electrical energy and that their presence causes a disruption in the surrounding energy field. Scientists argue that the devices are merely measuring normal background electromagnetic fields from sources including mobile phones, wiring and other electrical appliances.

Spirit box: A device used to scan AM/FM radio bands at high speed, creating a continuous stream of white-noise static and brief, disjointed fragments of music or human speech. The theory is that spirits can manipulate the changing radio frequencies and static to project their own voices. Sceptics argue that the device is merely picking up normal radio transmissions from local broadcasting towers.

Thermal cameras: Designed to detect invisible infrared radiation and convert it into colour-coded temperature maps, thermal cameras are used by paranormal investigators to search for localised drops in temperature. Some believe spirits draw energy from their surroundings and use the cameras to scan dark rooms in real time, looking for full-body thermal images or heat signatures that resemble human forms. Sceptics explain apparent ‘apparitions’ as the result of weather conditions causing natural temperature shifts or residual heat from a person or pet, which can linger and mimic a human figure.
